title: Rural Home Loans Escrow: Renewal Allowance on the Homeowner's Premium
content:
**Insurance desk note.** When the escrow of a Rural Home Loans loan is projected, the homeowner's insurance premium is projected with a renewal allowance.

## Rule

The homeowner's insurance premium is projected with a renewal allowance: the earlier premium is the homeowner's premium paid between 12 and 24 months before today, and when the latest homeowner's premium is at least 8 percent above that earlier premium, the allowance is 8 percent; when it is above the earlier premium by less than 8 percent, the allowance is 4 percent; when it is not above the earlier premium, or no homeowner's premium was paid between 12 and 24 months before today, there is no allowance; the projected premium is the latest premium increased by the allowance, rounded to the cent.

## Terms

- **Latest homeowner's premium:** the most recent homeowner's insurance disbursement paid from escrow.
- **Earlier premium:** the homeowner's insurance disbursements paid from escrow dated after the same calendar day 24 months before today and on or before the same calendar day 12 months before today, added together.

## Cases (hypothetical premiums)

| Earlier premium | Latest premium | Allowance | Projected premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000.00 | 1080.00 (exactly 8 percent above) | 8 percent | 1166.40 |
| 1000.00 | 1079.99 (just under 8 percent above) | 4 percent | 1123.19 |
| 1000.00 | 1000.00 (not above) | none | 1000.00 |
| none paid in the window | 1250.00 | none | 1250.00 |

## Point of reading

The allowance is a step, not a scale: any rise of at least 8 percent earns 8 percent, and any rise smaller than that, however close, earns 4 percent.
